subject: Cesium-5b elevated 5xx/timeouts — customer update & postmortem follow-up
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@brightsky.ai>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Cesium-5b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notice

Hi Sarah,

We observed an elevated rate of 5xx responses and downstream timeouts from Cesium-5b starting at ~08:45 PST this morning that may affect some of your inference traffic routed to the "cesium-stable" model tag. We’re actively investigating.

What we know so far:
- Error class: 5xx (internal server error) and model API timeouts (requests hitting the 10s backend cutoff)
- Affected tenant subset: customers routed to cesium-stable in us-west-2 (we see your traffic in that slice)
- Start window: ~2028-11-03T08:45:00-08:00

Immediate actions in progress:
1) We have throttled new long-context requests to Cesium-5b and enabled automatic fallback to Cesium-2b for compatible routes.
2) Infra is collecting kv-cache and kernel telemetry to surface root cause.
3) A rollback playbook is staged in case the trend persists (we will only execute with customer notice).

Please standby for a technical update within the next 90 minutes. If you'd like us to switch your production route to a fallback model proactively, say the word and we will initiate a controlled reroute + smoke tests.

Attachments: svc_health_dashboard.png (dashboard view), cesium5b_error_snippet.txt (sample 5xx stack snippet)

Apologies for the interruption — we’ll keep you updated.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-03T09:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cesium-5b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notice

Stephanie / Marcus,

Quick notes from runtime triage:
- We see a correlated kernel OOM on a subset of Cesium-5b shards when sequence lengths spike > 6k tokens. The memory pressure triggers the worker process to fail/restart which surfaces as 5xx.
- Frequency: ~1.8% of requests across the affected pool in the last 20m; spike aligns with several large-batch live jobs from a partner pipeline.
- Immediate mitigations enacted: autoscaler raised pool size (+2 nodes), per-request max-seq enforced at 6k, and fallback mapping to Cesium-2b enabled for routes with live LTS enabled.
- Logs attached (cesium5b_error_snippet.txt) with representative stack traces and process watchdog messages.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Temporary routing policy to limit long-context requests to dedicated capacity or fallback variants.
2) Patch to kernel allocator that reduces peak transient usage (we have a candidate; ETA for canary deploy ~6-8 hours).
3) Postmortem to capture rate-limiting and model-sizing guidance for customers.

I'll continue to monitor; will post another update after canary.

—Dylan
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@brightsky.ai>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-03T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Update: Cesium-5b incident — mitigation and recommended actions

Hi Sarah,

Quick update following infra triage:
- Root symptom: transient worker OOMs on Cesium-5b when individual requests exceed ~6000 tokens; this causes worker restarts and 5xx responses for in-flight requests.
- Mitigation taken: we enforced a temporary per-request token ceiling of 6000 on the affected pool and activated a routed fallback to Cesium-2b for routes flagged as latency-sensitive.
- Impact window observed so far: ~08:45–10:55 PST. Incident trend has largely stabilized after the mitigations.

Recommended actions for BrightSky team:
1) For high-throughput production endpoints, consider pinning to a fallback model family (Cesium-2b) for the next 24 hours while we stage the allocator patch.
2) If you rely on long-context requests (>6k tokens), please let us know so we can migrate you to Dedicated capacity where we can provision larger memory workers.

We’ve attached: rollback_playbook_v1.pdf (internal runbook excerpt) and the dashboard snapshot.

I’ll follow up tomorrow with a concise RCA and the timeline for the allocator patch. Regarding credit/SLA questions, we will evaluate the impact window and provide options as part of the post-incident package.

Do you want us to switch your production route to Cesium-2b now (we will run a quick canary and smoke test)?

Thanks for your patience — we know this is disruptive.

Best,
Stephanie
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@brightsky.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-03T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Update: Cesium-5b incident — mitigation and recommended actions

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the quick response and clear mitigation steps. A couple questions:

1) Can you confirm the exact impact window you will record for SLA purposes? We saw errors on several production jobs around 08:50–09:20 PST but the dashboard shows residual errors through ~10:55.
2) Please go ahead and switch our "text-infer-prod" route to Cesium-2b for the next 24 hours. We’ll monitor and provide feedback.

Also, can you summarize what guarantees or credits are available under the production SLA for this class of incident? We expect a short summary for our ops review.

—Sarah
Platform Engineering Lead
BrightSky AI
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@brightsky.ai>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-04T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Cesium-5b incident — RCA & postmortem follow-up

Hi Sarah — following up with the post-incident summary and our action plan. Thanks again for routing the change request; we completed the controlled reroute to Cesium-2b the same day and validated smoke tests.

Summary (RCA):
- Immediate cause: a combination of larger-than-expected per-request sequence lengths from a partner job and a transient regression in our kernel allocator that increased peak memory set size during kv-cache handling. The larger allocations caused worker process OOMs on Cesium-5b shards, leading to 5xx responses and timeouts for in-flight requests.
- Detection timeline: 08:45 PST anomaly surfaced; automatic health-slo alarms fired at 08:50 and infra mitigation actions began at 08:55. Stabilization occurred after token cap + fallback routing; residual errors cleared by ~10:55 PST.
- Impact window recorded for SLA: 2028-11-03T08:45:00-08:00 to 2028-11-03T10:55:00-08:00 (we will use the conservative window 08:45–10:55 PST for impact calculations).

Remediations and timeline:
1) Hotfix candidate for kernel allocator validated in staging — scheduled canary deployment to production 2028-11-05 02:00 UTC.
2) Longer-term fix: refactor allocator path to reduce transient peak by 40% (ETA Q1 2029).
3) New tenant-facing guidance: updated model-sizing docs and an automated suggestion in the Console to route long-context heavy workloads to Dedicated or fallback model variants.
4) Operational change: added an automated protective policy to cap per-request sequences to the highest safe level per model by default (configurable per-customer).

SLA/Credits:
- We will calculate the exact credit based on our SLA terms and the agreed impact window; expect a credit proposal within two business days.

Artifacts: attached: cesium5b_error_snippet.txt, svc_health_dashboard.png, rollback_playbook_v1.pdf; investigation ticket: https://console.redwood/investigations/INC-20281103-cesium5b

If you’d like a short postmortem call to walk through the technical details with your platform team, happy to schedule — suggest 30m tomorrow or early next week.

Again, apologies for the disruption. We’re prioritizing the canary and the automated protective policy to reduce recurrence risk.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
